memberdef.name: validateDatabaseCreateSchema

briefdescription.para: Validates a create (INSERT) request body against a table's schema.

detaileddescription.para:
tablename
Target table used for the schema lookup.
data
Parsed JSON body; must be a non-empty object.
error
Filled with code/message on failure; HTTP 400 for malformed input or missing/non-nullable columns, HTTP 400 for an unknown table.
rule
Per-key exceptions (e.g. ignore a server-generated "id").
True when the body satisfies all schema constraints.
Runs null/empty check, schema lookup, per-column type and nullability checks (checkColumns), and key-presence/prohibition checks (ensureAllKeysExist). Exceptions from jsoncons (such as a non-object body) are caught and reported as BAD_REQUEST, since these inputs are client errors rather than server faults.
validateDatabaseUpdateSchema, checkColumns, ensureAllKeysExist
See Validator::validateDatabaseCreateSchema. Processing order: reject null/empty input, resolve the table schema, validate present columns' types and missing non-nullable columns, then enforce per-key rules. The duplicated-key check is intentionally disabled because jsoncons parsing already rejects duplicate keys upstream.

memberdef.name: validateDatabaseUpdateSchema

briefdescription.para: Validates an update (PATCH/PUT) request body against a table's schema.

detaileddescription.para:
tablename
Target table used for the schema lookup.
data
Parsed JSON body; only a subset of columns needs to be present.
error
Filled with code/message on failure (HTTP 400).
rule
Per-key exceptions, notably ASSERT_IMMUTABLE for read-only columns.
True when the (partial) body is valid for an update.
Checks null/empty input and key-level constraints; unlike the create path it does not require every schema column to be present. Exceptions are translated to 400 for the same reasons as in validateDatabaseCreateSchema.

See Validator::validateDatabaseUpdateSchema. Unlike the create path, only keys actually present in the body are validated for type; there is no requirement that every schema column appear (partial updates are legal). Immutable/prohibited keys are still rejected through the rule in ensureAllKeysExist.

memberdef.name: validateDatabaseReadSchema

briefdescription.para: Validates the projected columns of a read (SELECT) request.

detaileddescription.para:
keys
Column names requested by the client.
table_name
Table the columns are requested from.
error
Filled with code/message on failure: 404 if the table has no schema, 400 if a key is prohibited by the rule or absent from the schema.
rule
Per-key exceptions, notably ASSERT_NOT_PRESENT for forbidden columns.
True when every requested key exists in the schema and none is prohibited.
See Validator::validateDatabaseReadSchema. Iterates the requested keys once, first applying ASSERT_NOT_PRESENT then checking membership in the cached schema. A key that is both prohibited and unknown is reported as prohibited; a missing table is reported as 404 rather than 400.

memberdef.name: clientRegexValidation

briefdescription.para: Applies field-specific regex rules to client-supplied entity data.

detaileddescription.para:
data
JSON object whose fields are validated by name (username, password, phone, email, dob, gender). Fields without a rule are passed through if they are non-empty strings.
error
Filled with 400 and a descriptive message on the first bad field.
db_data
Receives the validated (key, value) pairs ready for a database call.
True when all fields pass; false on the first invalid or empty value.
Regexes are compiled once into a function-local static map because compiling std::regex per request is expensive. A field with a validator must be a string, non-empty and match its pattern; an unvalidated field is copied only when it is a non-empty string.
Entries already present in db_data are preserved; results are inserted, not assigned.
See Validator::clientRegexValidation. Fields with a registered regex must be non-empty strings matching that pattern; unrecognised fields are accepted only if they are non-empty strings. The first offending field stops processing and fills error. Accepted pairs are inserted into db_data.

briefdescription.para: Rejects a null or empty JSON body as a client error.

detaileddescription.para:
data
Body to inspect.
error
Set to 400 / "Data is empty" when the check fails.
True when data is null or empty (i.e. validation should stop).
See Validator::nullCheck.

briefdescription.para: Looks up a table's cached column set.

detaileddescription.para:
tablename
Table to look up.
error
Set to 400 / "Table not found" when the schema is missing or empty.
found
Set true on success, false on failure.
A copy of the table's ColumnInfo set, or an empty set when not found.
The caller must consult found; an empty successful schema is treated as failure.
See Validator::getDatabaseSchemaForTable. Reads the process-wide schema snapshot via DatabaseSchema::getDatabaseSchema(). An absent table or an entry with no columns is treated as "not found" and sets found to false; the returned set is a copy so callers cannot mutate the cached schema.

briefdescription.para: Maps a PostgreSQL type name to a jsoncons type predicate.

detaileddescription.para:
value
JSON value to test.
expectedType
Schema type string (integer, float/double/real, character varying, boolean, jsonb, or date/time variants).
True when the JSON value's kind matches the schema type; false otherwise or for unrecognised type strings.
See Validator::validateType. "character varying" and all date/time spellings expect JSON strings; "jsonb" accepts either an object or an array. Date strings are not parsed here, only type-checked. Unknown schema type strings return false, which surfaces as a type mismatch to the caller.

memberdef.name: checkColumns

briefdescription.para: Checks each schema column against the body (create path).

detaileddescription.para:
data
JSON object under validation.
table_schema
Cached column definitions for the table.
error
Set to 400 on a missing non-nullable column or a type mismatch.
rule
Relaxations, notably IGNORE_IF_NOT_NULLABLE_IN_SCHEMA.
True when every column constraint is satisfied.
See Validator::checkColumns. Iterates schema columns (the authoritative source), not the body. A column that is absent is allowed when it is nullable or covered by IGNORE_IF_NOT_NULLABLE_IN_SCHEMA; a present column must match the schema's type according to validateType. The first violation aborts with HTTP 400.

memberdef.name: ensureAllKeysExist

briefdescription.para: Checks that every key in the body is permitted and known to the schema.

detaileddescription.para:
data
JSON object whose keys are checked.
table_schema
Cached column definitions used for the membership test.
error
Set to 400 on a prohibited, immutable or unknown key.
rule
Assertions and relaxations (ASSERT_NOT_PRESENT, ASSERT_IMMUTABLE, IGNORE_IF_MISSING_FROM_SCHEMA).
True when all keys are acceptable.
This checks keys in the data, not that all schema columns are present; the latter is enforced by checkColumns on the create path.
See Validator::ensureAllKeysExist. Builds a name set from the schema for O(1) membership tests, then scans the body. ASSERT_NOT_PRESENT and ASSERT_IMMUTABLE are checked first so prohibited/immutable keys are reported specifically; unknown keys are allowed only under IGNORE_IF_MISSING_FROM_SCHEMA.

briefdescription.para: Detects duplicate keys in a JSON object.

detaileddescription.para:
data
Object to scan.
error
Set to 400 with the duplicate key name when one is found.
True when a duplicate key is present.
Currently unused by the create/update validators: the jsoncons parser already rejects duplicate keys before these helpers run.
See Validator::hasDuplicateKeys. Uses a temporary set of key names; the first repeated name fills error and returns true. Kept for defensive use even though the JSON parser rejects duplicates first.

briefdescription.para: Stateless collection of checks applied to client JSON before it reaches the database.

detaileddescription.para: Entity controllers call these helpers with the parsed request body, the target table name and a Rule describing per-key exceptions. Validation is performed against a cached snapshot of the database schema (DatabaseSchema), not against a live query, so the helpers are cheap enough for the request path. Every entry point is static and reports failures by filling an api::v2::Http::Error (code + message) and returning false rather than throwing; exceptions from the JSON layer are caught and converted to 400 responses.

simplesect.para: All members are static; Validator carries no state and needs no lifetime management.
The cached schema must have been populated before these helpers are used, otherwise table lookups fail and the validators return false.
